summary: One POST form with an email address and a password at /account/login, on the connection's own origin. The same document carries a hidden one-time-password dialog for accounts that use 2-factor authentication.

sources.title: The public sign-in page of the original customer panel, rendered once without an account
Contabo knowledge base: How Do I Change My 2-Factor Authentication Settings? (last updated June 26, 2025)
sources.note: States that with 2-factor authentication on, the Customer Control Panel login takes the account secret and a one-time code generated by an authenticator application on the phone. Text only, no markup.

selectors.locator: frames[0], form#AccountLoginForm, its only input of type image (rendered)

selectors.note: The field exists in the first document but its dialog is closed. That the code is an authenticator code comes from the knowledge base article.

selectors.locator: frames[0], the button pane of the dialog that holds div#otp_login_dlg (not rendered)
selectors.note: A plain button outside form#otp_login_form: a script sends the code.

staysInteractive.note: Accounts with 2-factor authentication are asked for a one-time code after the first form. The steps file lists that dialog as an authenticator challenge; without a saved authenticator secret the user types the code.
The recovery code that replaces a lost authenticator, and any notice the panel shows after sign-in.

unverified: The page can change at any time and may differ by region or language. This is one anonymous render on the review date.
Nothing after the first form was observed, because no account was used: neither the result of the POST nor the page that follows it.
The one-time-password dialog was captured closed. When it opens, on which path, and that its button sends the form were not observed.
The form carries hidden request-token fields filled in by the server. That they are accepted when the fields are typed by the application was not tested.
A cookie notice is displayed on the first visit. Whether it covers the form was not determined.
The separate new.contabo.com panel is a different login and is not covered.
neededFromUser: One sign-in with this layout, with 2-factor authentication if the account uses it, or the sign-in page and the open one-time-password dialog saved as "Webpage, Complete". Save any page signed out and with no password typed in; keep the "_files" folder beside the .html and both outside the repository: they can hold the account name.
notes: Checked on the review date: robots.txt of my.contabo.com is readable and has Allow: /account/login; the terms and conditions (effective December 2025) are readable and have no clause on automated access or extraction, and neither has the legal notice, which was read after the capture. The capture was requested on my.contabo.com and ended on the same host and path. It loaded the page once and sent no input.
